question.:question/problem:
Evaluate the surface integral

$$
\iint_S \frac{3}{\sqrt{z-x+y^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}S
$$

where $S$ is defined by $z=x + y^{2} + 1$ for $1\le x\le 2$ and $-2\le y\le 2$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
For a surface $S$ defined by $z=g(x,y)$ with $(x,y)\in D,$ the surface integral of a scalar function $f(x,y,z)$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}f(x,y,g(x,y))\sqrt{1+{(\frac{∂z}{∂x})}^{2}+{(\frac{∂z}{∂y})}^{2}}\,\text{d}A.
$$

For the partial derivatives, we have

$$
\frac{∂z}{∂x}=\frac{∂}{∂x}(x + y^{2} + 1)=1,
$$

and

$$
\frac{∂z}{∂y}=\frac{∂}{∂y}(x + y^{2} + 1)=2 y.
$$

Therefore, the surface integral can be evaluated as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}\frac{3}{\sqrt{z-x+y^{2}}}\,\text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}f(x,y,g(x,y))\sqrt{1+{(\frac{∂z}{∂x})}^{2}+{(\frac{∂z}{∂y})}^{2}}\,\text{d}A\\ & ={∬}_{D}\frac{3}{\sqrt{\left(x + y^{2} + 1\right)-x+y^{2}}}\sqrt{1+\left(1\right)^{2}+\left(2 y\right)^{2}}\,\text{d}A\\ & ={∬}_{D}\frac{3}{\sqrt{2 y^{2} + 1}}\sqrt{4 y^{2} + 2}\,\text{d}A\\ & ={∬}_{D}\frac{3}{\sqrt{2 y^{2} + 1}}\sqrt{2\left(2 y^{2} + 1\right)}\,\text{d}A\\ & ={∬}_{D}\frac{3}{\sqrt{2 y^{2} + 1}}\sqrt{2}\sqrt{2 y^{2} + 1}\,\text{d}A\\ & ={∬}_{D}\frac{3}{\cancel{\sqrt{2 y^{2} + 1}}}\sqrt{2}\cancel{\sqrt{2 y^{2} + 1}}\,\text{d}A\\ & ={∬}_{D}3 \sqrt{2}\,\text{d}A\\ & =3 \sqrt{2}{∬}_{D}\,\text{d}A\\ & =3 \sqrt{2}\cdot\text{Area}(D)\\ & =3 \sqrt{2}\cdot\left(2-\left(1\right)\right)\cdot\left(2-\left(-2\right)\right)\\ & =3 \sqrt{2}\cdot\left(1\right)\cdot\left(4\right)\\ & =12 \sqrt{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
